title: Management of Chronic Asthma
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Asthma management should be an ongoing process of assessing, treating and reviewing the patient’s response.
The following factors should be addressed:
Correct inhaler technique should be demonstrated and checked regularly

Avoidance of triggers and other factors that could worsen asthma including: Exposure to Environmental Tobacco Smoke, Polluted environment (both indoors and outdoors) and Medications such as aspirin or NSAIDs, Avoid non- selective β-blockers,

blocks.text: Management of other medical conditions likely to affect asthma control such as cardiac disease, allergic rhinitis, obesity, Sleep Apnea and GERD.

blocks.text: Anti-asthma drugs can be classified as controllers (required for maintenance treatment) and relievers (required for quick relief, rescue drugs). Inhalers are the cornerstone of asthma therapy.

blocks.text: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) e.g. Beclometasone, budesonide, fluticasone
Long acting β2 agonists (LABA) e.g., formoterol, salmeterol: Inhalation 100mcg, 200mcg
Combined ICS-LABA: e.g., C: budesonide-formoterol (inhaler), C: Beclometasone-formoterol (inhaler),
Short acting β2 agonists (SABA) e.g. A: salbutamol inhaler 100-200 mcg PRN
Short acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA) e.g., B: Ipratropium bromide: 20 mcg/metered dose
There are two treatment approaches as follows

Low-dose ICS–formoterol taken as needed when symptoms occur, with or without maintenances ICS-Formoterol depending on severity. This strategy cannot be applied with other ICS-LABA combinations. It is specific to ICS-formoterol.
